summary: Germany is part of the Schengen Area: EU citizens travel freely, and Swiss and EEA nationals enter with a valid identity card or passport; nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorisation is not yet in operation), and nationals of the countries on its visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen short-stay visa (standard fee €90 under the Visa Code), applied for before entry at the German mission abroad covering their place of residence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Germany?
faq.answer: No. The United States is on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806), whose nationals can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Germany is among the countries that will require visa-exempt travellers to have an ETIAS travel authorisation, which is not yet in operation; the official ETIAS website gives the application fee as EUR 20.

faq.question: How much does a Germany Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged six to under 12. Under EU visa facilitation agreements, nationals of Armenia, Azerbaijan and Belarus pay €35 and nationals of Cabo Verde 75% of the standard fee. A national visa (category D) costs €75 under the Residence Ordinance, also for multiple entries. The Federal Foreign Office says Schengen visa holders can stay in the entire Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any period of 180 days.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Germany?
faq.answer: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The official ETIAS website gives the application fee as EUR 20.

faq.question: How can I move to Germany for work?
faq.answer: Germany's Federal Foreign Office says that if you intend to commence work in Germany you have to apply for a visa with the competent German mission abroad before entering Germany; only nationals of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea and the United States may apply for the necessary residence title after arrival. A national visa (category D) costs €75 under the Residence Ordinance (AufenthV § 46). No official source we could read here sets out the conditions of the EU Blue Card or the Opportunity Card.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Germany without a visa?
faq.answer: Nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and the Federal Foreign Office says visits to the Schengen Area by non-EU/EEA nationals are restricted to 90 days in any period of 180 days. EU law says no entry visa may be imposed on EU citizens; Swiss nationals enter on a valid identity card or passport under the EU–Swiss agreement, and the EEA Agreement incorporates the EU free movement directive.

Begründet der Inhaber einer in einem anderen Staat erteilten Fahrerlaubnis einen ordentlichen Wohnsitz im Inland, besteht die Berechtigung noch sechs Monate.

Ausländische nationale Führerscheine, die nicht in deutscher Sprache abgefasst sind, die nicht in einem anderen Mitgliedstaat der Europäischen Union oder einem anderen Vertragsstaat des Abkommens über den Europäischen Wirtschaftsraum oder der Schweiz ausgestellt worden sind oder die nicht dem Anhang 6 des Übereinkommens über den Straßenverkehr vom 8. November 1968 entsprechen, müssen mit einer Übersetzung verbunden sein, es sei denn, die Bundesrepublik Deutschland hat auf das Mitführen der Übersetzung verzichtet. November 1968 entsprechen, müssen mit einer Übersetzung verbunden sein, es sei denn, die Bundesrepublik Deutschland hat auf das Mitführen der Übersetzung verzichtet. Die Übersetzung muss von einem international anerkannten Automobilklub des Ausstellungsstaates oder einer vom Bundesministerium für Verkehr und digitale Infrastruktur bestimmten Stelle gefertigt sein.
